parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State Lenz’s law of electromagnetic induction.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
Two coils of insulated wire are wound on an iron bar, as shown in Fig. 8.1.

[[fig:f1]]

There is a current *I*₁ in coil 1 that varies with time *t* as shown in Fig. 8.2.

[[fig:f2]]
parts.text:
The variation with *t* of *I*₁ can be represented by the equation

*I*₁ = *X* sin *Yt*

where *X* and *Y* are constants.

Use Fig. 8.2 to determine the values of *X* and *Y*. Give units with your answers.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The current in coil 1 gives rise to a magnetic field in the iron bar. Assume that the flux density of this magnetic field is proportional to *I*₁.

An alternating electromotive force (e.m.f.) is induced across coil 2. The p.d. across coil 2 is measured using the voltmeter and has a root-mean-square (r.m.s) value of 4.6 V.

On Fig. 8.3, sketch a line to show the variation with *t* of *V*₂ between *t* = 0 and *t* = 0.08 s.

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Use the laws of electromagnetic induction to explain the shape of your line in (b)(ii).
